_meta.purpose: Per-enactment 'rules-as-of-last-verification' snapshot for the calc-time rule-freshness check. This metadata certifies that the modelling in the sibling rule files (bcsc-rules.md, bcca-rules.md, bc-arbitration-rules.md, limitation-rules.md) reflects each governing enactment as amended to the recorded signals. It MUST be bumped in the same commit as any rule-file update, so the two never desync. See vision.md Principle 5 and SKILL.md's rule-freshness workflow. A pending_changes[] entry also stays while any form in its `forms` list is not yet conformed (rule-freshness.md, Snapshot maintenance).
_meta.source: bclaws CiviX API (bclaws.gov.bc.ca) — no auth, King's Printer Licence. Fetch: GET /civix/document/id/complete/statreg/<id>. Catalogued in issue #114.
_meta.coarse_doc_id_note: The whole-enactment 'current to' string is fetched from coarse_doc_id when present, else civix_id. For multi-part enactments (the SCCR) a BARE civix_id fetch returns no currency string (confirmed live 2026-07-13, issue #160 build), which is why coarse_doc_id names the TOC part <civix_id>_00. The PART documents are not bare: 168_2009_01 carries both coarse signals ('current to July 21, 2026' and 'Last amended May 4, 2026 by B.C. Reg. 31/2026'), measured live 2026-07-28. An earlier reading of this note as 'only the TOC part carries the currency string' was wrong — a fetcher already holding a part document can read currency off it.

signals.currency_date: whole-enactment 'This consolidation is current to <date>' — coarse fast gate
signals.last_amending_reg: regulations only: 'Last amended <date> by B.C. Reg N/yyyy' — amending-instrument gate
signals.pit_watermark: top row (newest) effective date of the Point-in-Time table (<id>_pit) — section-level precise gate; null until first live fetch populates it
signals.pending_changes: enacted-but-not-yet-in-force amendments (ANIF folder / Gazette Part II) with commencement dates — forward look-ahead; each diarized as a /practice-data task. An entry's optional `forms` lists the official form numbers the amending instrument repeals, substitutes or adds, as strings; it is read by the litigation server's form-currency check (ADR 0038), never by this skill

Hastings Sunrise Development Ltd., 2008 BCSC 527; Cimolai v. British Columbia (Medical Services Commission), 2022 BCSC 528; Cimolai, 2022 BCCA 396; AES Engineering Ltd. v. Khan, 2021 BCSC 1384; and Jim Pattison Industries Ltd. v. 1854 Holdings Ltd. (1990), 52 B.C.L.R. (2d) 279 (C.A.). enactments.name: Interpretation Act
enactments._note: Governs the shared reckoning primitives (ss. 25, 25.2, 29) used across all proceeding rule files. Ticket #740 touched reckoning.md on 2026-09-20 and moved no signal: no live fetch was run and no consolidation re-read, so currency_date, pit_watermark and last_checked are unchanged. It added one paragraph to the Clear-day / exclusive counting section recording that s. 25.2 is assumed, not shown, to reach a period whose unit is the business day - s. 25.2(2) governs "a period of one day or consecutive days" and this Act defines no "business day", that term belonging to the governing Rules. The research closed with no authority either way, so the assumption stands and is now labelled wherever it is relied on. This is the shared statement loaded with every rule file, so the caveat reaches the Court of Appeal and Supreme Court business-day rows alike. Full record: Engineering/bcca-appeal-books-inputs/research-findings-740.md. Recorded for the atomicity invariant. Ticket #746 touched reckoning.md again on 2026-09-21 and likewise moved no signal: no live fetch was run and no consolidation re-read, so currency_date, pit_watermark and last_checked are unchanged. It appended one paragraph to the Clear-day / exclusive counting section confirming the #740 assumption as permanent. The research routes are exhausted: five decisions were retrieved and read in full, and the legal-research gate reports no located authority at any level deciding whether s. 25.2 reaches a period whose unit is the business day, either way, so the assumption is unsupported by authority and uncontradicted by authority. Two limits on the located set matter for this Act. FIRST: the two months cases in it, Coyle 2008 BCSC 527 and Jim Pattison (1990) 52 B.C.L.R. (2d) 279 (C.A.), engage s. 25.3 and not s. 25.2, and Jim Pattison construes the repealed R.S.B.C. 1979, c. 206, s. 25(4)-(5), whose relationship to the present s. 25.2(2)-(3) is NOT verified by anyone on this ticket and is not relied on; the 1979 provision excludes first and last days from a count, whereas s. 25.2(3) shifts an endpoint by one day, so they are textually related but not the same rule. SECOND: AES Engineering Ltd. v. Khan, 2021 BCSC 1384 quotes todays numbering, not pre-renumbering numbering, and its quoted text of ss. 25(3) and 25(4) is word for word the current Act, so the unverified-renumbering caveat attaches to Coyle and Jim Pattison but not to AES. One proposition from AES at paras. 24-26, adopted in Cimolai 2022 BCSC 528 at para. 29, is judicially settled and confirms from authority the structural point #740 made from the text alone: this Act has no machinery for excluding non-working days from a count, its non-working-day provisions operating only where a period begins or ends on such a day and then only by shifting that endpoint. That proposition is BCSC level and unreviewed, is confined to forward counting, and expressly does not reach s. 25.2(3). Full record: Engineering/bcca-appeal-books-inputs/research-findings-746.md. Recorded for the atomicity invariant.
